topic: Forefoot pain and burning toes (Morton's neuroma)

slides.headline: Burning between your toes when you walk?
slides.sub: Forefoot pain and Morton's neuroma, in plain English.

slides.title: What it usually is
slides.body: Morton's neuroma is an irritated, thickened nerve between the long bones of the foot, most often between the third and fourth toes. It's common and often settles with simple changes.

slides.title: What it often feels like
slides.body: Burning, tingling or numbness into the toes, or a feeling like standing on a pebble or a folded sock. Taking your shoe off and rubbing the foot often eases it.

slides.title: Give your toes room
slides.body: Narrow, pointed or high-heeled shoes squeeze the forefoot. Try shoes with a wider toe box, a lower heel and decent cushioning, and loosen the laces across the front.

slides.title: Other things that can help
slides.body: A metatarsal pad placed just behind the sore spot can spread the pressure. Adjusting your walking or running load, plus calf and foot strength work, often helps too.

slides.title: When to get it checked
slides.body: Constant numbness, swelling or redness, pain that wakes you at night, or symptoms that aren't easing after a few weeks of shoe changes are worth an assessment.

slides.headline: Walk more comfortably again
slides.body: Our Sydney CBD and Chatswood physios assess your feet, footwear and loading, then build a plan to settle your symptoms. Book online — link in bio.

caption:
Feels like you're walking on a pebble, or a folded sock, under the ball of your foot?

Burning or tingling between the toes, often the third and fourth, can come from an irritated nerve known as Morton's neuroma. It's common, and many people improve with fairly simple changes.

Start with your shoes: a wider toe box, a lower heel and laces loosened across the front give the forefoot room. A metatarsal pad, adjusting your walking or running load, and calf and foot strengthening can help too. Constant numbness, swelling or night pain are worth getting checked.
